captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Signed-form certification boundary.  Negative finite-endpoint forms
and the rank-340 mixed spectrum remain certifiable in deep tails.  The exact
rank-4 Laplace control remains numerically accurate but fails the current
analytic COS-series certificate because its Fourier decay is much slower.
captions.caption_markdown: Signed-form certification boundary. Negative finite-endpoint forms and the rank-340 mixed spectrum remain certifiable in deep tails. The exact rank-4 Laplace control remains numerically accurate but fails the current analytic COS-series certificate because its Fourier decay is much slower.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Independent noncentral controls.  Three scaled isotropic Gaussian
quadratic forms with different dimensions and noncentralities were compared
against SciPy's noncentral-\(\chi^2\) law from \(10^{-4}\) through
\(10^{-40}\).  The largest observed discrepancy was approximately
\(9.3\times10^{-15}\) decades, with all analytic truncation certificates
passing.
captions.caption_markdown: Independent noncentral controls. Three scaled isotropic Gaussian quadratic forms with different dimensions and noncentralities were compared against SciPy’s noncentral-$\chi^2$ law from $10^{-4}$ through $10^{-40}$. The largest observed discrepancy was approximately $9.3\times10^{-15}$ decades, with all analytic truncation certificates passing.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Demonstrated precision envelope across positive analytic controls,
a production-scale rank-1997 spectrum, corrected strong-dependence spectra,
signed finite-endpoint and mixed-sign forms, and noncentral exact controls.  Points whose stored benchmark difference rounded to zero are
placed at $10^{-16}$ decades only to make them visible on the logarithmic
vertical axis.
captions.caption_markdown: Demonstrated precision envelope across positive analytic controls, a production-scale rank-1997 spectrum, corrected strong-dependence spectra, signed finite-endpoint and mixed-sign forms, and noncentral exact controls. Points whose stored benchmark difference rounded to zero are placed at $10^{-16}$ decades only to make them visible on the logarithmic vertical axis.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Independent direct-inversion validation near $p=10^{-16}$ on four
heterogeneous spectra.  Circles show the relative K-COS/inversion difference;
crosses show the analytic bound on the inversion integral omitted beyond the
final truncation point.
captions.caption_markdown: Independent direct-inversion validation near $p=10^{-16}$ on four heterogeneous spectra. Circles show the relative K-COS/inversion difference; crosses show the analytic bound on the inversion integral omitted beyond the final truncation point.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Width of the directed-rounding K-COS probability enclosure on exact
scaled-chi-square controls.  The enclosure remains narrow even at
$10^{-5000}$.
captions.caption_markdown: Width of the directed-rounding K-COS probability enclosure on exact scaled-chi-square controls. The enclosure remains narrow even at $10^{-5000}$.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Arithmetic versus analytic uncertainty at a $10^{-5000}$ tail.  The
directed-rounding arithmetic enclosure becomes negligible; the final width is
controlled by the explicit analytic support and series remainders.
captions.caption_markdown: Arithmetic versus analytic uncertainty at a $10^{-5000}$ tail. The directed-rounding arithmetic enclosure becomes negligible; the final width is controlled by the explicit analytic support and series remainders.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Accuracy-driven refinement.  Each point lies at or below the
requested-equals-achieved line because an interval result is labeled certified only
after the requested multiplicative probability accuracy has been proved.
captions.caption_markdown: Accuracy-driven refinement. Each point lies at or below the requested-equals-achieved line because an interval result is labeled certified only after the requested multiplicative probability accuracy has been proved.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Residualization is the geometric starting point. Every sample-space vector splits into a component in the covariate span and an orthogonal residual component. The factor $A=M_XGW^{1/2}$ therefore acts only on variation remaining after the null-model covariates have been removed.
captions.caption_markdown: Residualization is the geometric starting point. Every sample-space vector splits into a component in the covariate span and an orthogonal residual component. The factor $A=M_XGW^{1/2}$ therefore acts only on variation remaining after the null-model covariates have been removed.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Exact block-kernel assembly. The sample interaction kernel carried by each resident variant block is $K_b=A_bA_b^\top$, and the full kernel is their exact sum. Streaming changes the order of evaluation, not the operator.
captions.caption_markdown: Exact block-kernel assembly. The sample interaction kernel carried by each resident variant block is $K_b=A_bA_b^\top$, and the full kernel is their exact sum. Streaming changes the order of evaluation, not the operator.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Partition-refinement invariance in floating-point tests. Coarse, fine, irregular, singleton-heavy, and permuted blockings reproduce the explicitly formed Gram matrix and its action to machine precision. The block schedule is therefore an execution choice rather than a change in the statistical model.
captions.caption_markdown: Partition-refinement invariance in floating-point tests. Coarse, fine, irregular, singleton-heavy, and permuted blockings reproduce the explicitly formed Gram matrix and its action to machine precision. The block schedule is therefore an execution choice rather than a change in the statistical model.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: The exact polyphase light cone. The support of the Krylov iterate expands by at most one graph edge per operator application. Phases outside graph distance $k$ remain identically inactive at depth $k$ and need not be loaded.
captions.caption_markdown: The exact polyphase light cone. The support of the Krylov iterate expands by at most one graph edge per operator application. Phases outside graph distance $k$ remain identically inactive at depth $k$ and need not be loaded.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Weak long-range phase couplings replace the exact zero outside the retained light cone by a nonzero but certified envelope.  In this PSD test, the phasewise transfer-matrix certificate bounds the observed leakage at every depth from one through eight.
captions.caption_markdown: Weak long-range phase couplings replace the exact zero outside the retained light cone by a nonzero but certified envelope. In this PSD test, the phasewise transfer-matrix certificate bounds the observed leakage at every depth from one through eight.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Certified phase-graph sparsification at Krylov depth five.  Retaining fewer off-diagonal phase blocks reduces communication and operator work while the transfer-matrix bound remains above the measured truncation error.  The bound is intentionally conservative because it ignores cancellation and singular-vector alignment.
captions.caption_markdown: Certified phase-graph sparsification at Krylov depth five. Retaining fewer off-diagonal phase blocks reduces communication and operator work while the transfer-matrix bound remains above the measured truncation error. The bound is intentionally conservative because it ignores cancellation and singular-vector alignment.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Depth-five pruning under a fixed certified error budget.  A global block-norm threshold is nearly unable to prune this example without crossing the requested tolerance, whereas query-aware edge risks remove many phase pairs.  The exact-envelope refinement safely uses slack left by the additive majorant.
captions.caption_markdown: Depth-five pruning under a fixed certified error budget. A global block-norm threshold is nearly unable to prune this example without crossing the requested tolerance, whereas query-aware edge risks remove many phase pairs. The exact-envelope refinement safely uses slack left by the additive majorant.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Raw phase-block magnitude and finite-depth query risk are different quantities.  The edge score $\beta_{hg}^{(5)}$ incorporates the start profile and every depth-five transfer path through the phase graph; the block norm $\mathcal B_{hg}$ does not.
captions.caption_markdown: Raw phase-block magnitude and finite-depth query risk are different quantities. The edge score $\beta_{hg}^{(5)}$ incorporates the start profile and every depth-five transfer path through the phase graph; the block norm $\mathcal B_{hg}$ does not.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Idealized effect of asynchronous double buffering over $64$ streamed blocks.  The largest modeled speedup occurs when transfer and computation times are comparable, because neither resource is left idle for most of the pipeline.  The additional cost is one extra resident block buffer.
captions.caption_markdown: Idealized effect of asynchronous double buffering over $64$ streamed blocks. The largest modeled speedup occurs when transfer and computation times are comparable, because neither resource is left idle for most of the pipeline. The additional cost is one extra resident block buffer.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: Phase-local rank as a dimension law. The archived six-phase audit records constructed rank, numerical rank and minimum exact width of one through six, with the remaining capacity wasted by a uniform width of twelve. A rank-revealing factorization keeps the new directions. This summary replaces an annotated singular-value curve whose raw plotted vector was not archived.
captions.caption_markdown: Phase-local rank as a dimension law. The archived six-phase audit records constructed rank, numerical rank and minimum exact width of one through six, with the remaining capacity wasted by a uniform width of twelve. A rank-revealing factorization keeps the new directions. This summary replaces an annotated singular-value curve whose raw plotted vector was not archived.

captions.canonical_caption_tex: QR-core spectral equivalence under the stated orthonormality hypotheses. The diagram pairs the exact factor identity with the archived maximum absolute and relative \(\ell_2\) singular-spectrum discrepancies for a 128-row factor with 180 old and 37 appended columns. Recorded audit metrics replace the overlaid singular-value curves, whose raw vectors were not archived.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Dual-budget phase pruning.  The query-local budget controls Krylov
propagation while the operator budget controls final spectral and tail
uncertainty.  A loose operator budget can admit a strong coupling and widen
the tail interval by several decades even when the Krylov-local budget still
passes.
captions.caption_markdown: Dual-budget phase pruning. The query-local budget controls Krylov propagation while the operator budget controls final spectral and tail uncertainty. A loose operator budget can admit a strong coupling and widen the tail interval by several decades even when the Krylov-local budget still passes.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Certify-after-prune range residual.  The range-core theorem is valid
at every depth, but a deep-tail full-spectrum guarantee can remain useless
until the range residual is genuinely small.  This negative result is retained
as a stopping-rule lesson rather than hidden as an implementation failure.
captions.caption_markdown: Certify-after-prune range residual. The range-core theorem is valid at every depth, but a deep-tail full-spectrum guarantee can remain useless until the range residual is genuinely small. This negative result is retained as a stopping-rule lesson rather than hidden as an implementation failure.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Incomplete-range tail certification before exact completion.  The
trace/moment bound preserves the amount and concentration of unresolved
spectral mass instead of shifting every coefficient by one worst-case radius.
captions.caption_markdown: Incomplete-range tail certification before exact completion. The trace/moment bound preserves the amount and concentration of unresolved spectral mass instead of shifting every coefficient by one worst-case radius.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Residual-rank certification in the full-rank stress test.  From depth
3 onward the moment lower bound meets the orthogonal-complement upper bound.
At depth 8 exactly two residual directions remain.
captions.caption_markdown: Residual-rank certification in the full-rank stress test. From depth 3 onward the moment lower bound meets the orthogonal-complement upper bound. At depth 8 exactly two residual directions remain.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
LD structure changes the effective spectral rank.  The corrected
copy-LD models create much stronger local dependence than the latent-Gaussian
moderate-LD case, while all remain within the same streamed SKAT pipeline.
captions.caption_markdown: LD structure changes the effective spectral rank. The corrected copy-LD models create much stronger local dependence than the latent-Gaussian moderate-LD case, while all remain within the same streamed SKAT pipeline.

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Raw-genotype streaming reproduces the materialized SKAT kernel across
multiple LD regimes and block sizes.  The observed discrepancies are at

K-COS versus the high-resolution full-spectrum tilted reference on

captions.canonical_caption_tex:
Reference-convergence audit.  The adaptive certified answer remains
stable while an initially under-resolved fixed-grid reference converges toward
it.  A single nominally large reference grid is therefore not treated as
authoritative without its own refinement check.
captions.caption_markdown: Reference-convergence audit. The adaptive certified answer remains stable while an initially under-resolved fixed-grid reference converges toward it. A single nominally large reference grid is therefore not treated as authoritative without its own refinement check.

unavailable original eigenvalue vector.
